critical_code_review_comments: EnforcePortalScope.jsx Iter149-revised policy is correct and minimal: PAIRS-loop only clears a token when pathname === a DIFFERENT portal's login path (LOGIN_PATHS map). Cross-portal browsing now preserves tokens.
Master-directory sessions still correctly bypassed via authorizedPortals() / dirHas() guard.

Token-bearer guard ordering is sound: RequireSafety/RequireHr renders AccessDenied on first paint based on isSignedInAnywhere(); EnforcePortalScope useEffect runs after but no longer mutates the token on cross-portal namespaces, so the post-paint state is stable.
No additional issues observed in AccessDenied.jsx, permissions.js, Hub.jsx — all unchanged from Iter149 and behaving as specified.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iter149 token-preservation regression is fully resolved. EnforcePortalScope now uses an explicit LOGIN_PATHS pathname-equality check before clearing any token. T1 anonymous-hub assertion uses data-testid prefix 'hub-section-*' (not 'hub-portal-*' — that was a wrong selector in iter149's raw output but the underlying behaviour was always correct). No console errors observed throughout the full multi-portal session. No further action needed for this iteration.
rca_of_the_issue: Original bug (iter149): EnforcePortalScope cleared the user's portal token whenever pathname left that portal's URL scope, racing with RequireXxx → AccessDenied first-paint render and stranding the user. Fix applied: EnforcePortalScope only clears a token now if pathname === a DIFFERENT portal's specific /login path (LOGIN_PATHS map). All other navigation (cross-portal namespace browsing, refresh, deep-link, hub home) preserves the token. The fix is verified across both directions: cross-portal browsing (preserves token, AccessDenied works) and explicit cross-portal sign-in attempt at /hr/login while holding a safety token (correctly clears safety token, allowing the new portal sign-in to take over).
